historical_reported_context.scope: The historical pair used the same 100-second workload on each version. It provides one observation per version and lacks stage markers. The current 19-second phases with mirrored repetitions form a separate comparison.

baseline_provenance.scope: The 0.1.1 production web package was reproduced exactly. Its freshly compiled native host is labeled as a rebuild.

prior_sustained_attempt.later_native_samples: visible and foreground before scheduled restore

windows_native_capabilities.requestValidation: fixed empty request accepted; unexpected selector rejected

windows_desktop_smoke.method: Independent WebView2 profiles. Launch-to-first-result measured through the UI using a test-only CDP session. Sum of working sets can include shared pages. CDP offline mode was applied after startup.

method_limits: Mirrored launch order uses isolated WebView profiles and a fixed 19-second same-prefix workload. The completed prefix lengths differ. The focused timing comparison uses the same 50 triplets for each version.
JavaScript/WASM memory counts and process-tree counters cover overlapping but unequal scopes. Shared pages may appear in more than one process count.
System-wide memory changes include unrelated Windows activity. Exact allocator, runtime cache and retained mathematical state allocations cannot be recovered from these counters.
Next animation frame measures a renderer timing boundary. It does not establish GPU presentation latency. OS scheduling and DevTools protocol overhead are not individually traced.
Each worker startup count describes the available observation per run. Startup measurements are descriptive where sample counts do not support an upper-tail estimate.
The direct and forced probes supplement the normal Playwright click and checked result waits.
